headline: One Teacher's Simple Affirmation Practice Transforms An Entire School
meta_description: A Kansas first-grade teacher's daily positive affirmations have spread across Rex Elementary School, creating a culture of safety and belonging.
summary_short: Tyler Richards' daily affirmation practice at Rex Elementary School in Haysville, Kansas, has inspired teachers across all grades to adopt similar approaches.
body:
At Rex Elementary School in Haysville, Kansas, first-grade teacher Tyler Richards has sparked an unexpected transformation—one rooted not in complex intervention but in the power of simple, spoken affirmations. Each day, his classroom fills with young voices declaring truths: "I am kind!" and "I can do hard things." What began as one educator's effort to send children home feeling valued has now rippled across the entire school, with teachers at multiple grade levels implementing their own versions of the practice. Principal Shane Paulus credits the initiative with helping students feel genuinely welcomed and appreciated, offering them a positive emotional foundation as they leave school each day.

The real measure of success, Paulus notes, is how quickly children have claimed ownership of the practice themselves, generating fresh ideas for how to incorporate affirmations into their daily routines. Rather than remaining a top-down directive, the strategy has become something the students actively shape and champion. For Richards, the deeper purpose extends beyond the moment of speaking the words. These affirmations serve as an anchor, helping children transition from the school day into whatever comes next—whether that's heading home or moving to an after-school activity—with their sense of safety and capability intact.

What makes this story remarkable is not the novelty of positive self-talk, but its humble, organic spread. Richards understands that educators hope to leave a lasting imprint on their students' lives, and he recognized that consistency matters more than complexity. By building these few minutes into the daily rhythm, he created space for children to internalize belonging. As the practice continues to expand across grade levels, Rex Elementary has quietly become a place where affirmation is not something students receive occasionally, but something that defines the culture itself.
quick_facts: Tyler Richards teaches first grade at Rex Elementary in Haysville, Kansas
Daily affirmations like "I can do hard things" are now spreading across multiple grade levels
Principal Shane Paulus reports students are actively creating new ways to implement the practice
The affirmations help children transition from school to home or activities with positivity
